sources.quote: 10% cashback, up to INR1,200 a month, on all dining, food delivery, grocery, shopping and utility spends
Shopping spends on Amazon, Flipkart & Myntra merchants continue to earn 1.5% cashback
1.5% unlimited cashback* on most other spends

examples.title: Rs 2,000 restaurant bill
examples.why: 10% cashback on dining: 2000 x 10% = 200, counts towards the Rs 1,200 per month cap on the 10% tier.

examples.title: Rs 5,000 grocery spend
examples.why: 10% on grocery: 500, counts to the Rs 1,200 per month limit.

examples.title: Rs 10,000 other spend (hotel)
examples.why: 1.5% unlimited on most other spends: 10,000 x 1.5% = 150.

examples.title: Rs 2,000 dining with Rs 1,100 of the 10% cap already earned
examples.why: 10% would be 200 but only Rs 100 of the Rs 1,200 monthly cap remains.

examples.title: Rs 2,000 dining after the Rs 1,200 monthly cap is used
examples.why: HSBC worked example: 10% tier Rs 41,500 earns 4,150 capped at 1,200 and the total is 1,200 + 345 (1.5% tier) = 1,545, so spend over the cap earns nothing extra.

examples.title: Rs 3,000 fuel
examples.why: The page example table shows 0% cashback on fuel.

research_notes.cardpipeline_says: liveplus-accelerated-cap: eligible_spend Rs 10,000 per statement cycle, then base 1.5%
research_notes.issuer_says: Issuer: 10% cashback up to INR 1,200 a month (cashback, not spend). Spend above the cap earns nothing extra per the HSBC worked example.

research_notes.cardpipeline_says: MCC list of dining, food and grocery only
research_notes.issuer_says: Issuer page and guide say 10% applies to dining, food delivery, grocery, shopping and utility spends; "shopping" is not defined, with Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra excluded from the 10%. CardPipeline omits shopping and utility, which under-states the card; left unmodelled (never widen).
Guide: 1.5% cashback will no longer be earned on international spends (forex markup 1.99%, lounge changes from 1 Sep 2026).
research_notes.proposed_fix: importer: international exclusion needs a currency/geography field

research_notes.cardpipeline_says: rent/insurance MCC exclusions in the source
research_notes.issuer_says: The HSBC pages retrieved say only that the 1.5% tier has exclusions without listing them; no issuer text found for rent and insurance, so no examples are written for them.
